title: Bata India Ltd - 500043 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bata India Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 4% to INR979 crore, with underlying PBT up about 22% and gross margin up 130 bps.
summary.overview: Bata reported Q1 FY27 turnover of INR979 crore, up about 4% YoY, with volume and price contributing roughly equally to growth. Underlying PBT grew about 22%, and the company crossed 2,000 EBO stores. Management flagged raw material cost push of 5-6% (mainly crude-linked synthetics), which it plans to offset through price increases that reach shelves from around September. Monsoon-related deferral of revenue in the prior quarter was expected to reverse in July and early August. The call was an Ambit-hosted post-earnings session, with management declining forward guidance.

segments.name: Bata brand (ladies)
segments.commentary: Ladies category was the lead driver within Bata brand, supported by the Taapsee Pannu campaign and the Everyday Essential range. Bata grew despite the adverse trend.

segments.name: Hush Puppies
segments.commentary: Led growth alongside Floatz, with strong sequential and YoY growth; no figure was disclosed.

segments.name: Floatz
segments.commentary: Continued strong sequential and YoY growth; no figure disclosed.

segments.name: Power / NorthStar (sneakers)
segments.commentary: Power grew well; NorthStar was a drag as lines are being rationalised ahead of a stronger collection over the next couple of quarters.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: Broad-based growth across ZBM stores (close to 800 stores, about 80% of business), franchise (about 750 stores), e-commerce and multi-brand outlets. Franchise and e-commerce carry lower gross margin but are EBIT-accretive.

guidance_outlook: No forward-looking revenue guidance given; management described itself as 'reasonably optimistic'.
Cost push of 5-6% expected to be offset by price increases; management expects no margin dilution from cost push in subsequent quarters.
Price-hiked stock expected to reach markets at scale around September 2026.
Product funnel reimagination expected to show more impact in H2 FY27 and H1 FY28; significant portfolio change by March 2027.
Gross margin levers cited: premiumisation and higher full-price sales; channel mix (franchise/e-commerce growth) a partial offset.

Vendor consolidation: from about 100-120 partners 2.5-3 years ago to below 70 (about 60) now; target of 15 core plus 15 satellite partners over 3-5 years, with total margin benefit about 200 bps over that period.
Elevated marketing spend expected to continue for the next couple of years; ZBM 2.0 (Project Elevate) results to be shared next quarter.
capex_capacity: Store network: about 2,000 EBO stores crossed, of which about 1,250 COCO/DOS (incl. about 125 Hush Puppies DOS) and about 750 franchise; management aspires to 3,000 stores over time.
Franchise potential trade areas identified: in excess of 600.
Store clutter: average lines per store at 68% of level two years ago; management sees the optimal level near 60%.
Stock turns at about 2.5+, moving towards 2.7; inventory held at about 140-150 days.
demand_pricing: Lower price points showing some resurgence after GST rationalisation about three quarters ago; premium segment still growing faster and ASP has risen.
Raw material cost push of about 5-6%, mainly imported synthetics (crude derivatives); similar price increases taken on new and existing products.
Competitive intensity at lower price points too early to call; management believes many peers have not yet absorbed full raw material inflation.
Franchise like-for-like growth close to high single digits for about the last four quarters.
Full-price sales near 89-90% with markdowns falling.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation was faced and how is it being mitigated?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost push of about 5-6% from synthetics; not yet visible in Q1 because of 140-150 days of inventory. Price increases taken; margin dilution not expected in subsequent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin not expand more despite higher full-price sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix (franchise and e-commerce growing faster) diluted gross margin by about 100 bps. Without it, gross margin expansion would have been about 230 bps versus 130 bps reported; EBIT per pair is the benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores, and what is the ZBM contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1,250 COCO/DOS and about 750 franchise stores. About 775 ZBM stores generate about 80% of COCO retail revenue; management sees ZBM near saturation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost flat for five quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: VRS was part of the business case; a 24-month organisational restructuring, Blue Yonder merchandising platform and manpower reallocation drove savings. Store manpower broadly unchanged; franchise growth required added manpower.

qa_highlights.question: Franchise store economics and SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise like-for-like growth close to high single digits for about four quarters. Partner ROI about 18-24%. Revenue per sq ft not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: A&P trajectory and timing of revenue payback?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P at about 3-3.5% of sales vs about 2.5% a year ago; management said it will not move to 7-8%. Revenue payback expected 'as early as possible'.

risks_watch: Pass-through of 5-6% cost push: price-hiked stock reaches markets around September; watch realisations and volumes in Q2.
Lower price-point competition and consumer pushback as peers absorb raw material inflation.
Gross margin dilution from faster franchise and e-commerce growth offsetting premiumisation and full-price gains.
NorthStar sneakers drag until the rationalised collection arrives over the next couple of quarters.
Rising A&P (about 3-3.5% of sales) must translate into double-digit top-line growth; timeline unspecified.
Store clutter reduction (target about 60% of lines per store) must not hurt conversion.
Senior management transition: a participant wished Gunjan Shah well for future endeavours, implying a possible CEO change; not confirmed on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating levers (full-price sales, inventory, ZBM, franchise, cost restructuring) but cautious on near-term top-line and inflation pass-through, repeatedly declining numeric guidance and deferring to 'wait and watch'. Gross margin and revenue targets were answered qualitatively.
